method: Rebuild from primary text. Labor Code §§2870, 2871 and 2872 were fetched in full from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and the clause body was rewritten from what those sections say. The construing case was located through CourtListener. Assertions below describe the REBUILT body; the previous body's errors are under priorDefects.
queries: "Labor Code section 2870" invention assignment employee "own time"

assertions.text: the carve-out covers an invention developed entirely on the employee's own time without using the employer's equipment, supplies, facilities, or trade secret information
assertions.note: §2870(a), verbatim. 'Entirely' does real work and is carried.

assertions.text: the first exception applies to an invention that relates, at the time of conception or reduction to practice, to the employer's business or actual or demonstrably anticipated research or development
assertions.note: §2870(a)(1). The previous body dropped 'at the time of conception or reduction to practice', which is the clock the comparison is made against; without it the exception floats and can be argued from any later date.

assertions.text: the second exception applies to an invention that results from any work performed by the employee for the employer
a provision purporting to require assignment of an invention the carve-out excludes is against the public policy of California and unenforceable
assertions.note: §2870(b), added by Stats. 1991, Ch. 647: 'To the extent a provision in an employment agreement purports to require an employee to assign an invention otherwise excluded from being required to be assigned under subdivision (a), the provision is against the public policy of this state and is unenforceable.' The previous body stated the carve-out but not this consequence.

assertions.text: an employer may not require a provision made void by §2870 as a condition of employment or continued employment
assertions.note: §2871, first sentence. Absent from the previous body.

assertions.text: the written notification duty comes from §2872 and attaches to employment agreements entered into after January 1, 1980
assertions.note: §2872: 'If an employment agreement entered into after January 1, 1980, contains a provision requiring the employee to assign or offer to assign any of his or her rights in any invention to his or her employer, the employer must also, at the time the agreement is made, provide a written notification to the employee that the agreement does not apply to an invention which qualifies fully under the provisions of Section 2870.' The previous body said the notice was 'given under California Labor Code §2870'. It is not; §2870 defines the excluded inventions and imposes no notice duty.

assertions.text: the employee claiming the benefit of §2870 bears the burden of proof
assertions.note: §2872, final sentence, and expressly held in Cubic Corp. v. Marty. Absent from the previous body, and it is the allocation that decides most disputes under the section.

assertions.text: the notification must be given at the time the agreement is made
assertions.note: §2872: 'the employer must also, at the time the agreement is made, provide a written notification'. Timing, not merely content.

priorDefects: contradicted: 'This notice is given under California Labor Code §2870.' The notification duty is §2872; §2870 imposes none.
omitted: 'at the time of conception or reduction to practice' from the first exception (§2870(a)(1)).
omitted: §2870(b), that an overbroad assignment provision is against public policy and unenforceable.
omitted: §2871, that the employer may not require such a provision as a condition of employment or continued employment.
omitted: §2872's burden of proof on the employee and the after-January-1-1980 scope.

scope: §§2870-2872 speak to employees and employment agreements. The clause sits in a founder IP assignment and addressed 'the founder'; a founder who is not an employee may fall outside the article entirely.
gaps: The clause is inserted when opState is CA or TX (condition unchanged by this rebuild), but its body states California law only. No Texas provision was read and Texas has no counterpart to §2870 that this session verified. For a Texas operation the clause currently recites law that does not govern. This is unresolved and is the most serious thing left in it.
Whether a non-employee founder is within §§2870-2872 was not resolved from primary text. The rebuilt body names the employee scope so the reader can see the question, but it does not answer it.

§2871's proviso — that an employer may still require disclosure in confidence, a review process, and full title in the United States where a federal contract requires it — is recorded here but not carried into the clause body, because the clause is a notice to the worker rather than a statement of employer rights.

singleOpinionCaveat: Cubic Corp. v. Marty predates the 1991 addition of §2870(b), so it does not speak to the unenforceability consequence. It is relied on here only for the burden-of-proof allocation, which it states directly and which §2872 also states in terms.
